title: Dynamic credential cooldown orchestration — runbook draft
summary: Runbook draft for dynamic per-credential cooldown orchestration with circuit-breaker behavior to mitigate bursty abuse from leaked keys while preserving healthy tenant throughput.
content:
Context:
This is a working runbook for handling incidents where a subset of API keys or tenants produce sudden high-rate traffic consistent with credential leakage or automated scraping. The goal is to provide a graduated response that: (1) contains the abusive traffic quickly, (2) minimizes collateral impact to adjacent tenants, and (3) creates a reproducible automation path so oncall can act quickly without manual key rotation for every incident.

Why this is different: current fast-path playbooks are either global throttles or full key revocation. Both extremes either cause excessive app-level disruption or require heavy manual ops. This draft proposes a coordinated cooldown window, progressive circuit-breaker thresholds, and automated temporary token suspension with safe fallback routing.

Detection signals (composite):
- sudden per-key request rate > 10x historical median for that key over 15m AND
- token new-IP entropy: > 30% of requests from IPs not seen for that token in last 7d OR rapid geo fanout (>3 regions in 10 minutes) AND
- error profile skew: high 4xx (401/403) or repetitive identical prompt payloads (indicator scanning)
- telemetry spike on application-side: late-stage LLM rejection/failure loops (increased retry count)

Initial triage (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm with dashboards: per-key rate chart, IP distribution, linked customer contact. Link to quick-query: QUERY_KEY_TRAFFIC(<key>) -> returns 1m/5m/15m rates and top 10 IPs.
2) Correlate with recent deploys or infra changes (check release-engineering slack and CI tags). If deploys present within last 30m, tag incident as "deploy-related" and follow deploy rollback checklist.
3) If signal meets composite threshold, start the "credential-cooldown" incident in PagerDuty and notify product-security.

Immediate actions (manual, low-friction):
- Step A: Apply soft cooldown (recommended default) -> limit token to 2x baseline throughput but keep route open. Use the API: POST /admin/tokens/<key>/limits {"rate": "soft-2x", "window": "15m", "reason": "cooldown-suspected-leak"}.
- Step B: Enable temporary IP allowlist/denylist on WAF for the top 3 abusive IPs pending forensic review. Do NOT global-block until confirm.
- Step C: Turn on request sampling for that token at 100% and increase log retention for 24 hours to collect full payloads (for legal/product review).

Automated escalation (what to trigger if cooldown doesn't reduce abuse):
- After 10 minutes of soft-cooldown, if request rate > 5x historical median OR new IPs continue arriving, transition to progressive circuit-breaker: incrementally reduce rate to 1x -> 0.5x -> 0.1x on 5m intervals.
- If circuit-breaker reaches 0.1x and abuse persists, trigger temporary token suspension with auto-rotation: call automation: POST /ops/rotate-token {"token_id": "<key>", "mode": "temporary-suspend-and-rotate", "notify": ["owner","eng-sre"]}. Automation will: create replacement token, mark old token as suspended, provision replacement to customer owner via secure channel, and attach a rollback TTL of 24h.

Fallback routing:
- For customers using Hosted API with failover to Dedicated or alternate regional endpoints, if token suspension occurs, the system will apply a per-tenant fallback policy to route authenticated requests to read-only embedding endpoints where possible (non-generation paths). This preserves customer visibility while preventing abuse-driven generation costs.

WAF interplay guidance:
- Prefer targeted WAF rules keyed by IP ranges + UA fingerprint, not broad-based rules that affect entire region.
- When adding WAF exceptions, annotate rule with incident id and the reason. Example WAF note: "INC-2026-0041: temporary block 18.205.93.0/24 - matched repeated token spray patterns".
- Keep a rolling list of "safelist test IPs" to ensure WAF rules are tested before enforcement.

Customer communication and security handoff:
- If token rotation or suspension happens, CS must send templated notification: short explanation, mitigation actions taken, instructions to rotate keys on their side (if applicable), and offer 24h support window. Template link: Confluence/DynamicTokenTemplates.
- If evidence of data exfiltration or PII access is suspected, immediately escalate to security@redwood and follow the formal incident response checklist (forensics imaging, preserve logs).

Forensics checklist (post-containment):
- Export top 1k request logs for the token, preserving original timestamps and IPs.
- Capture runtime metrics for model invocations during the attack window: token latency, GPU utilization, KV-cache hit ratio.
- Collect sample prompts and deduplicate. Flag those that look like credential-stuffing, scraping, or injection attempts.
- Run IP reputation lookup and add to evidence bundle.

Testing and exercises (SRE-run):
- Quarterly tabletop: simulate a leaked-token scenario using a non-prod token and ramp traffic using internal loadgen. Verify the cooldown automation transitions through soft->circuit->suspend without impacting other tenants.
- Chaos test: randomly inject NAT IPs from 5 source regions to confirm geo-detection heuristics.
- Smoke test: run the full rotation automation in staging and verify notification flow to CS and that rollback TTL correctly re-enables token when requested.

Runbook CLI snippets (for oncall):
- Quick view top IPs for token: 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_API_KEY" 
    "https://telemetry.internal/api/token-traffic?token=<key>&window=15m" | jq .top_ips
- Apply soft cooldown: 
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"rate":"soft-2x","window":"15m","reason":"cooldown-suspected-leak"}' 
    https://admin.internal/api/tokens/<key>/limits
- Trigger rotation automation (manual override): 
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_API_KEY" -d '{"token_id":"<key>","mode":"temporary-suspend-and-rotate","notify":["owner","eng-sre"]}' https://ops.internal/api/rotate-token

Manual escalation criteria (when to ring human):
- Evidence of cross-tenant lateral movement (same IPs hitting multiple unrelated tokens)
- Sustained cost delta > $1k per hour attributable to the token after 30 minutes of automated controls
- Legal or regulatory signal (customer says they are seeing user data in requests or suspected PII).

Post-incident follow-ups (action items):
- Short-term (assigned within 48h): run a telemetry correctness audit for signal thresholds, tune geo-fanout and IP-entropy thresholds. Owner: Liam O'Connor.
- Medium-term (2 weeks): build synthetic canary to validate soft->suspend transitions in CI. Owner: Chen Wei.
- Long-term (quarter): evaluate offering an opt-in forensic mode for customers with high-risk data that provides stronger per-request provenance and easier rotation UX. Owner: Product-Security.

Metrics to capture for continuous improvement:
- Mean time to containment (MTC) in minutes from detection to soft-cooldown and to full suspension.
- False positive rate (customer-impactful suspensions / total suspensions).
- Cost saved per incident (estimate avoided generation tokens billed to infra).

Open questions / TODOs in this draft:
- Exact numeric thresholds for soft vs hard cooldown need A/B testing in production (suggest starting conservative to avoid customer disruption).
- How to best surface rotation actions to customers using Managed Dedicated with their own key store? Need product input.
- Legal constraints on storing sampled request payloads for 24h (confirm with compliance).

Notes to self / oncall hints: keep change windows small, annotate every temporary WAF and token action with incident id, and prefer short-lived automated rotations rather than blanket revocations. This runbook should live next to the fast-path automations but separate enough to emphasize credential-specific heuristics.

References and links:
- Incident query macro: QUERY_KEY_TRAFFIC (internal)
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Dynamic+Token+Cooldown+Design
- Related automation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1332
- Template customer communications: Confluence/DynamicTokenTemplates

End of draft.
